chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī and Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from a man, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
A man who goes out from the Haram for some need—he said: if he returns in the same month in which he left, he may enter without ihram; but if he enters in another month, he enters with ihram.

key_terms.الشَّهْرِ: the month used as the legal time boundary in this ruling
key_terms.الْحَاجَةِ: a need or necessity for which one goes out
key_terms.بِإِحْرَامٍ: in the state of ihram required for entry
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ إِحْرَامٍ: without entering the consecrated state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Does someone who leaves the Haram and returns to Makkah have to enter with ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about re-entering Makkah after leaving the Haram for a need. It states that returning within the same month does not require ihram, whereas returning in a different month requires entering in ihram.
